We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude. We had a lease, and when the lease was almost up, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, but left a few things and a note saying he didn't want to bring those things with him. The thing is, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and they can take money from your deposit for that. I've heard of people losing $250 just because someone had to take three milk crates of their stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, "Why not sell them?" There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party where he was also there. We were being polite, and then he asked how the move-out process went. I told him it was good, and naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing I can be held accountable for, but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Okay, so I need to figure out if I did the right thing or not. Let's break it down. First, when he moved out, he left some stuff behind. By the terms of our lease, I think it's standard that if you leave stuff behind, the landlord can dispose of it, and you might lose part of your deposit. So, in that sense, I was trying to help him by contacting him to pick up his stuff. But he didn't respond. So, I took the initiative to get rid of his stuff to prevent him from losing money from his deposit. But then, I sold his video games and made $600 from it. Is that okay? I mean, legally, it seems like there's nothing wrong with it because he abandoned the stuff, and I was just disposing of it. But morally, is it right to sell someone else's stuff without their permission, even if they abandoned it? I think about the principle of "finders keepers." If someone abandons their property, does that mean I can take ownership of it? Or is there an obligation to try to return it or at least get permission before selling it? Also, I tried to contact him, but he didn't respond. Does that mean I have the right to dispose of his stuff as I see fit? Or should I have made more efforts to reach him, like going to his new place or something? Another thing to consider is the value of the games. $600 is a significant amount. If I had just thrown them away, that would have been one thing, but selling them for money adds another layer to it. Is it fair to keep the money, or should I give it to him since it's from his stuff? I also think about the relationship aspect. He's now calling me an asshole and asking for the money back. Even if legally I don't have to give it back, should I consider his feelings and maybe offer him some compensation to keep the peace? On the other hand, I feel like I did the right thing by trying to contact him and prevent him from losing money from his deposit. If I had just thrown his stuff away, that would have been worse. By selling the games, I actually made money that could have potentially gone to the landlord if they had to dispose of it. So, in a way, I saved him money. But still, selling his stuff without his permission feels a bit invasive. It's his property, even if he left it behind. Maybe I should have at least tried to find another way to return it to him or get his permission before selling. I'm also thinking about the concept of abandonment. If someone leaves their stuff behind, does that mean they've abandoned it, and I can do whatever I want with it? Or is there a certain period after which it's considered abandoned? In this case, he left the stuff a few years ago, and I only sold them recently. So, maybe legally, it's considered abandoned, but morally, it's still his stuff. I guess it's a gray area. Another angle is the intention behind my actions. I tried to contact him, and when he didn't respond, I took action to prevent him from losing money. My intention was to help him, not to profit from his stuff. But by selling the games, I ended up making money, which might make it seem like I took advantage of the situation. I also wonder about the value of the games. If they were just a few games, it might be different, but 60 games is a lot. Maybe I should have made an effort to find him again or at least inform him before selling them. In the end, I think I did what I thought was right at the time, but it's causing some conflict now. Maybe I should have handled it differently, like holding onto the games longer or finding another way to return them to him. But I also don't want to be responsible for someone else's stuff indefinitely. Overall, I'm conflicted about whether I did the right thing or not. Legally, it seems fine, but morally, it's a bit murky. I need to decide whether to keep the money or give it back to him to maintain the relationship, even if I'm not legally obligated to.
